First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{7\pi }{8}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{7\pi }{8}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8}) & =7\cdot (2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{8})) \\  & =7\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
